sections.h2: Which office in Rutherfordton files Rutherford County deeds?
sections.html:
The Rutherford County Register of Deeds works from 229 North Main Street in Rutherfordton. Postal mail goes to Post Office Box 551, Rutherfordton, NC 28139. Per the county, the counter is staffed from half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted.

Two phone lines are published: 828-287-6155 for the main desk and 828-287-6195 for the record room. The county says its holdings reach back into the 1700s, which is useful context for anyone selling a family tract that has passed through many hands in the foothills.

Most sellers never visit in person, because the attorney or title agent delivers the deed. Still, a rejected deed delays the closing and the payout, so the rules are worth knowing.

sections.h2: What papers does Rutherford County keep besides deeds?
sections.html:
The county lists a wide range of public records in its Rutherford register collection:

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust, with their cancellations
  • Assumed names and powers of attorney
  • Road maintenance agreements and plats
  • Separation agreements and similar filings

An online index lets you search by name. A separate alert tool named Property Check emails you when something new is filed against a name or parcel you choose. Heirs watching a house that sits empty can use it to spot an unexpected lien or a forged transfer early.

sections.h2: How must a deed be formatted for the Rutherford County clerk?
sections.html:
Under section 161-14, the county lists layout rules that a deed must meet on the page. Hold your draft up against each one:

  • Page one of a deed or deed of trust carries the preparer's name.
  • Paper is 8.5 inches wide and either 11 or 14 inches long.
  • Page one keeps its upper three inches empty, and every other edge needs at least half an inch of white space.
  • Text prints black on white, at 9 points or larger, on one side of each sheet.
  • The kind of instrument is spelled out across the head of page one.

Blanks and corrections may be inked in by hand. Having your attorney read the draft before signing is the least costly way to dodge a rejected filing.

sections.h2: Will late property tax stop a Rutherford County deed from recording?
sections.html:
It will. The register of deeds cites section 161-10(a)(19), effective October 1, 2011, which makes payment of delinquent taxes a condition of recording.

A tax lien explains the rule. Under section 105-355 it fastens to the property on the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs fasten with it. If the debt goes unpaid, a foreclosure auction can follow, and a person who redeems before confirmation must pay all of it (section 105-374).

Request a written balance for every parcel from the Rutherford County revenue office before you sign a contract, so your attorney can clear it from the sale money.

sections.h2: What fees does the Rutherford County recorder collect?
sections.html:
The statewide schedule in section 161-10 governs. On top of that, the county says military discharges are recorded free and satisfactions of deeds of trust carry no charge.

Recording charges at the Rutherford County desk

Under the statute these are the only charges, and they are due before anything is filed.

sections.h2: What excise tax rides on a Rutherford County deed?
sections.html:
The charge is one dollar per $500 of price or value, with leftover dollars rounded up to the next $500 block, and sellers settle it before the deed is filed (section 105-228.30). The county keeps one half and the state receives the other.

A sale for cash is a transfer for value, so the tax is owed. Your attorney can show it as a separate line item.

Land that spans two counties is taxed in whichever county holds more of the value. If your Rutherford tract crosses a county line, raise it with your attorney early.

The statute lets the county retain a small slice of the state half as an allowance, which is bookkeeping between governments.

sections.h2: Where does a Rutherford County seller get a tax balance?
sections.html:
The county revenue department answers tax bill questions at 828-287-6000 and sits at 145 College Avenue, Suite A, Rutherfordton, NC 28139, and the counter hours there match, half past eight to five A collections email address is posted on the same department page.

The department page says all tax bills are due September 1 each year, and that payment by January 5 avoids interest and enforced collection. Mailed payments are honored by postmark through that date. Cash or check payments are taken at the tax office, while online payment runs through a third-party service that adds its own fees, whose amounts the vendor determines.

The page also shows a search for tax bill information, a link to registered vehicle tax receipts, and a list of delinquent tax bills. Pull your parcel's bill and ask for a payoff before your closing attorney orders the deed.

The department also posts a tax rate document. Because the total bill depends on the fire district and town where the house sits, ask the office which rates apply to your parcel instead of assuming a countywide figure. Phone 828-287-6000 and have the parcel number ready.

sections.h2: Does the Rutherford County office file business name certificates?
sections.html:
Yes. The register of deeds records assumed business name certificates, the doing-business-as forms that tell the public a person or firm trades under a particular name in one county or in all 100 North Carolina counties. The recording fee printed on the county page is $26.00.

An online option exists for businesses located in Rutherford County, with a $15.00 service fee added to the recording fee. The county also notes that certificates recorded before December 1, 2017 expired on December 1, 2022, so an older DBA for a rental or landlord business needs a fresh filing. Landlords with rentals should make sure a business name used on leases is still on file.

sections.h2: Does Rutherford County accept electronic filing?
sections.html:
Yes. The county notes that e-recording through Simplifile began in the office on April 24, 2018, with plats added on February 1, 2022. It also states that microfilming began January 1, 2017.

Speed matters because registration time sets rank. A deed or long lease binds lien creditors and later purchasers for value only from the moment it is registered, and the earlier filing wins (section 47-18). When a buyer's lender and a seller's lender both file on closing day, a same-day electronic filing keeps your deal clean.

Anyone unsure about a particular document can call the main desk at 828-287-6155 before sending it.

faqs.q: What days is the Rutherford County recorder open?
faqs.a: Half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted, per the county. The main line is 828-287-6155. Calling first avoids a wasted trip on a holiday week.

faqs.q: Is filing a deed of trust satisfaction free in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county page says no charge applies to satisfactions, and state law agrees. Make sure your lender files one after payoff.

faqs.q: Who owes deed excise tax when a Rutherford County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller does. Section 105-228.30 sets one dollar per $500, collected ahead of filing, and the settlement statement should show it as its own entry.

faqs.q: Can overdue taxes hold up my Rutherford County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Under section 161-10(a)(19), as the county explains, back taxes come first. Obtain the balance from the revenue office and pay it at closing.

faqs.q: Does Rutherford County take electronic recordings?
faqs.a: Yes. E-recording via Simplifile started April 24, 2018, and plat e-recording started February 1, 2022. Title companies and attorneys generally use it.
